sections.title: Booking a local history walking tour

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: I can reserve your place on the short history walk. This route looks at the way the streets were used before the new buildings went up.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: What should I write for the tour code?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Your booking code is H24. It is H followed by two four.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And what is the day of the walk?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: The walk is on Friday. The weekend tours visit a different part of the town.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Could you confirm the meeting time?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: We will meet at 9:35, or twenty-five to ten. The guide will start checking the list a few minutes earlier.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: What have you put down for the meeting point beside the?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Meet by the fountain. The steps outside the hall are used by the longer tour.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: What should I write for the guide’s surname?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Your guide is Sutton. The name on the notice is spelled with two Ts.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And what is the route leaflet colour?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Collect the cream leaflet. The green one gives a route for people walking without a guide.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Could you confirm the first stop at the old?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: The first stop is at the old market. We will pass the library later, on the way back.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: What have you put down for the walk duration?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: The route takes about fifty minutes. That includes a short stop to look at a street plan.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: What should I write for the additional item to bring?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Bring a pencil if you would like to mark the old street names on the leaflet.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And what is the end point near the?

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: The walk ends near the arch. From there, you can return to the meeting point in a few minutes.

script.speaker: Tour assistant
script.text: Your confirmation gives the meeting point and the route code. Let us know if you need to cancel so we can offer the place to someone else.

sections.title: A route through a field study centre

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Welcome to the field study centre. The path junction in the middle is your reference point. North is at the top, and all the marked routes return to this point.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The weather station is north of the junction, beyond the top path. It stands on an open patch of ground.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The stream table is east of the junction. The right-hand path leads to the covered bench where it is set out.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The soil shelter is south of the junction, close to the bottom of the plan. It contains samples from different parts of the site.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The tool store is west of the junction, behind the gate on the left. Keep the doorway clear when you collect equipment.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Keep the soil in its trays. The labels can be read without lifting material from them.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Put each observation in the log. Write the time beside the reading before going to the next station.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The water is moved by a small pump. Ask the instructor before changing the speed.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Gloves are available in the tool store. Choose a pair that fits before starting the activity.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Eat lunch beside the central junction. Food should be kept away from the sample trays.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The discussion starts at two o’clock. Return a little earlier if you have equipment to hand in.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The last group will come back to the junction for a short discussion. Return the borrowed equipment before you leave the centre.

sections.title: Designing a trial of wind barriers

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: The group has built two small wind barriers for a class demonstration. We want to observe how the position of the barrier changes the movement of air behind it.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: All right. Let’s go through the details.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Start by comparing air speed behind the barrier. We will note the shape of the supports, but the main outcome is not the colour or the weight of the model.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Keep the fan setting the same. The barrier position will change and the readings can differ.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Put the first sensor at the centre of the marked line. The left end and the right end will be used for later readings.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Jules will prepare the supports. Sana will mark the measuring points, and Nia will check the record.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Sana will mark the measuring points on the bench. The sensor should return to each mark in the same position.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Nia will check the first record before we change the arrangement. She can ask for a repeat if an entry is unclear.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Use a ruler for the distance from the fan. Estimate the position only after the marks have been put down.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Keep the sensor at the same height. Air can move differently near the bench and higher up.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Wait ten seconds after switching on the fan, then take the first reading.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Use a different letter for each barrier. That makes the results easier to find when the models are put away.

script.speaker: Jules
script.text: Keep both sets of readings. If one position looks unusual, we can repeat it before saying which arrangement gives better shelter.

sections.title: How a plant support affects growth

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A climbing plant can use a support to reach a new part of the space around it. Today we will compare two supports and decide what observations would make their effects clear.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Choose plants of a similar size at the start. Keep a photograph so that you can compare them later.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Measure from the pot’s edge when placing a support. Use the same starting position for the two arrangements.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The first support is a wooden stake. It gives the plant a single upright line.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: The other support has several horizontal strings. Record when the plant first reaches one.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Use a removable label to mark a fixed reference point. Do not attach it to a part that grows.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Note the direction of the main stem at each visit. The plant may grow sideways before it grows higher.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Give the same amount of water to each pot. The aim is to compare the supports rather than water supply.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Take each photograph from the same side. Mark the position so you can find it again.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Hold a ruler beside any stem extending beyond the support. This gives a scale for the photograph.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Record damage caused by strong wind if it occurs. It can change the appearance of growth without being an effect of the support.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: A single measurement of final height is only one piece of evidence. Include the shape of the support, the position of the plant and what happened over time.
